skeptic.argument: Thirteen findings over six screens, and three of the nine units in the inventory have never been opened. Two of those three have paths that do not resolve to anything on disk and the third has no path at all, which means the enumeration itself is the least trustworthy artefact in this session. Nothing here should be called converged until that is settled one way or the other.

builder.argument: The empty and error states are the same defect wearing three hats: every screen renders its success case and treats absence as if it cannot happen. That is one shared component and an afternoon, not four separate tickets, and saying so changes how the plan should be ordered.

empath.argument: Ranking by reach times stakes times recoverability puts the thread error first — it is the screen a person reaches from a shared link, and a bare 403 tells them nothing about whether to ask for access or give up. The compose undo window is second: high stakes, and today entirely unrecoverable.

dreamer.argument: Read the six graded screens as three columns — empty, loading, error — and the shape of the product appears. Every screen has a success case, four have no empty state, and exactly one has any error handling at all. The holes are not scattered; the whole non-success half of this product was never designed.
